title: TF-IDF & BM25
interviewAnswer: TF-IDF weights terms by within-document frequency and corpus rarity. BM25 adds saturation and document-length normalization, making it a strong lexical ranking baseline.
keyPoints: Lexical search handles exact names/codes well.
why: TF-IDF & BM25 appears frequently in data-science work because it connects mathematical assumptions to practical decisions, diagnostics and failure modes.
deepDive: TF-IDF weights terms by within-document frequency and corpus rarity. BM25 adds saturation and document-length normalization, making it a strong lexical ranking baseline. BM25 term-frequency gain saturates. Lexical search handles exact names/codes well. A strong practitioner separates the modeling assumption from the estimation procedure, checks diagnostics rather than trusting a single score, and explains what would make the method inappropriate.
workedExample: A query containing a rare error code should strongly match documents containing that exact code.
commonMistakes: Applying the method without checking its assumptions or data-generating process.
Choosing it because it is familiar rather than comparing against an appropriate baseline.
followUps: What assumptions does TF-IDF & BM25 make?
How would you validate or debug TF-IDF & BM25 in practice?
production: In production, validate assumptions on real data, monitor the quantities that can drift, and keep a simple baseline so added complexity has a measurable reason to exist.

lab.goal: Implement a tiny BM25 scorer and compare lexical ranking.
lab.buildIt:
import math,re
docs=['red bolt m8 stainless','blue bolt m6 steel','m8 stainless anchor bolt']
q='m8 stainless bolt'.split()
tok=[re.findall(r'\w+',doc.lower()) for doc in docs]
N=len(tok); avg=sum(map(len,tok))/N
def bm25(i,k1=1.5,b=.75):
    s=0.0
    for term in q:
        df=sum(term in x for x in tok)
        idf=math.log(1+(N-df+.5)/(df+.5))
        tf=tok[i].count(term)
        if tf:
            s+=idf*tf*(k1+1)/(tf+k1*(1-b+b*len(tok[i])/avg))
    return s
print([bm25(i) for i in range(N)])
lab.useIt:
from sklearn.feature_extraction.text import TfidfVectorizer
from sklearn.metrics.pairwise import cosine_similarity
v=TfidfVectorizer().fit(docs+[' '.join(q)])
M=v.transform(docs); qq=v.transform([' '.join(q)])
print(cosine_similarity(qq,M)[0])
lab.shipIt: Keep lexical retrieval as a production baseline even with vectors; exact identifiers, rare codes and filters often benefit from BM25/hybrid search.
